questions.question: What does the overhead inside rearview mirror do?

options.text: Lets the driver see inside the bus.
Lets the driver see outside the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets the driver see inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror on a school bus lets the driver watch what passengers are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: If a student drops an item while walking to a school bus, what should they do?

options.text: Stop and pick up the object.
Have another student pick up the object.
Ask the driver to pick up the object.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick up the object.
questions.explanation: If a student picks up a dropped object, the driver may not see them. This is dangerous. Instead, students should move away from the bus, get the driver's attention, and let the driver pick up the item.

questions.question: When doing a driver's side parallel parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pass the parking space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the parking space without passing it first.
Back into the parking space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on the left side of your vehicle, then back into it. Bring the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle should fit completely within the boundaries of the space.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you can lose points by:

options.text: Exiting the vehicle one time to check your positioning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing over an exercise boundary.
questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses an exercise boundary line. Each time your vehicle crosses a line, you lose points on your skills test score.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which is an example of poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Driving in the left lane when more than one lane is available
Finishing a right turn in the right lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in the left lane when more than one lane is available
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, keep your vehicle between lane markings. Stop behind stop lines and crosswalks. On roads with multiple lanes, complete turns in the correct lane. Stay in or move to the right lane unless it is blocked.

questions.question: How far ahead of a school bus stop should the flashing lights turn on?
questions.correctAnswerText: At least 200 feet
questions.explanation: School buses with flashing amber warning lights should turn them on at least 200 feet before the bus stops, unless state law says otherwise.

questions.question: When exiting a bus, a driver must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the handrail.
questions.explanation: When exiting during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. If testing in a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in automatic failure.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which gear usage mistake should you avoid?

options.text: Selecting a gear that does not rev the engine
Forgetting to shift through an intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: Shifting while taking a turn
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine. Avoid grinding gears. Do not shift while turning or going through intersections.

questions.question: While students board or leave the bus, the driver should:

options.text: Watch the students and monitor the loading and unloading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the students and monitor the loading and unloading.
questions.explanation: The driver should watch students as they enter or exit to make sure they don't get caught in the door or handrails. The driver should also make sure students move safely away from the bus after they exit.

questions.question: What should a properly adjusted outside convex mirror show?

options.text: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts
The rear door of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts
questions.explanation: On a school bus, outside convex mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see one traffic lane on each side of the bus, the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

questions.question: When picking up students, park at least 10 feet away from them. Why?

options.text: You can see their movements clearly.
It is hard to get closer to the students.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see their movements clearly.
questions.explanation: Park with your front bumper at least 10 feet from students. This is safest because students must walk to the bus. The driver can watch them the whole time.

questions.question: Students are being unloaded when other students cause trouble on the bus. What should you do?

options.text: Walk to the back of the bus and fix the problem while students unload.
Wait until all students are off the bus, then fix the problem.
Have another student handle it while you watch the unloading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until all students are off the bus, then fix the problem.
questions.explanation: Loading and unloading students requires your full attention. If there is a behavior problem, wait until all students have safely exited the bus before addressing it.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror is used to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Watch passengers inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The inside rearview mirror helps you watch what students are doing on the bus.

questions.question: On the expressway during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors to see traffic.
Drive on the left side of your lane.
Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors to see traffic.
questions.explanation: On the expressway, keep your position in the lane and proper distance from other vehicles. Stay at the posted speed limit. Check your mirrors often to see traffic around you.

questions.question: When picking up students, stop ____ away from them.
questions.correctAnswerText: At least 10 feet
questions.explanation: Stop at least 10 feet from students at a bus stop. This makes students walk toward the bus, so you can watch where they are.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, adjust mirrors:
questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Always check and adjust all mirrors before you drive the bus.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not stop.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass other vehicles, or change lanes while crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: To safely unload a bus, students should:

options.text: Stay seated until told to exit.
Stand up and head to the door while the bus is slowing down.
Exit and stand next to the bus while it drives away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay seated until told to exit.
questions.explanation: Students must stay seated until the driver tells them it is safe to exit. After leaving the bus, they should walk at least 10 feet away so the driver can see them clearly.

questions.question: Danger zones on a school bus are located:

options.text: Only in front of the bus.
Only in the rear and on the left side.
In front, on the sides, and in the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front, on the sides, and in the rear.
questions.explanation: Danger zones are areas where children are most likely to be hit by the bus or another vehicle. These zones are in front, on the sides, and in the rear. Danger zones extend about 10 feet from every side of the bus.

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse at a pick-up point, you should:

options.text: Back up before students board the bus.
Back up after students board the bus.
Back up while students guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up after students board the bus.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous and should be avoided. If you must back up at a pick-up point, wait until all students have boarded the bus first.
